title: Two Bodies, One Warmth
logline: Through one year in a shared household, a grandchild visibly grows and a great-grandparent visibly slows, fed and warmed by the same table, the same well, the same weather.

object.note: Object 7 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: From a body being assembled to two bodies at opposite ends of one life: a child growing and a great-grandparent slowing at the same table through one year.

thread_out.thread: The slowing that the year shows reaches its end: after a death, a village funeral-aid society takes over the practical work so a family can sit with its loss.

requirements: A multi-generation household willing to be visited repeatedly across a full year
Ongoing consent from every generation, renewed at each visit
A household where an infant or young child and an elder both live together

suggestions.name: A multi-generation household in a hill-country or Uva village
suggestions.why: Extended, multi-generation households living under one roof remain common in these regions; no specific family is identified.

lesson.in_simple_terms: The texts say the same warmth that helps a child grow is what slowly wears an older body down. Ageing was there all along; grey hair is only its sign.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: දරුවෙකු වඩන උණුසුමම වැඩිහිටි ශරීරයක් සෙමින් දිරවන බවත්, දිරීම මුල සිටම පැවති අතර හිසකෙස් පැසීම එහි ලකුණක් පමණක් බවත් අභිධර්මය කියයි.
lesson.the_teaching: The fire element, heat and cold, is described as ripening: it builds and strengthens bodies and it also wears them down, which is why a body grows and later weakens. The Margaya puts it plainly: in youth, ripening makes matter mature and grow, and once maturing is complete, repeated ripening makes bodies and outside things decay, so one and the same element brings both growth and decline. Among the characteristics of matter, decay belongs to all matter once it has arisen; in childhood growth is so visible that decay goes unseen, and grey hair, fallen teeth and wrinkles are not decay itself but only signs that it has happened.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: Through one year at the same table and the same well, the film sets the child's crawling, first words and first steps beside the elder's slowing pace, a good day and a hard one, in evening routines that repeat with small differences. Seen across the seasons, both changes come from the same meals, weather and warmth, and the viewer can notice this without a word of commentary.

key_terms.en: fire element: heat and cold; ripening

lesson.caution: This is not a promise that a good attitude keeps anyone young, and the texts' reckoning of how long matter lasts is a doctrinal model, not a measurement of ageing.
lesson.builds_on: The midwife's film watched a body being built; this one follows the warmth that builds a child as it wears an elder down, so growth and decay are seen as one process.
